WHAT EXISTS · WHERE IT IS · WHO HOLDS IT

Research outputs

Three degrees of research, a consultancy, an internship and code on GitHub: some of it public, some held by the organisations it was done for, the rest a PDF I will happily send you.

This page says which is which — because a portfolio that lists outputs without saying whether anyone can read them is a list of assertions.

  • 10 public
  • 3 on request
  • 3 held by the client

Public: open it now. On request: it exists and I hold it — ask. Held by the client: it belongs to the organisation it was made for. No entry names a journal, a conference or a DOI, because none of this work has one.

Public

Code 2026 Public

Groundwater Investigation Toolkit

Python and browser code for rural borehole projects in Sierra Leone: resistivity soundings, drilling logs, pumping tests and water quality in; figures, borehole designs and .docx reports out. The repo links a browser app.

A toolkit dated 2026, not the records of my 2018–2019 fieldwork. Its worked examples are partly illustrative or synthetic, as the repo says. Read the case study →

Framework 2026 Public

GAIA Framework 2.2 — Green AI Assessment

An open (MIT) framework, Excel workbook and web estimator for the energy, carbon and water footprint of an organisation's AI use, with uncertainty tiers. It maps its outputs to disclosure lines in GRI, ESRS E1 and E3, IFRS S2, CDP and SBTi.

A mapping to disclosure line items, not a claim of compliance. Its estimator weighs workloads typed into it and cannot read actual usage. Read the case study →

Code 2026 Public

climatematch-pipeline — climate extremes for West Africa

A Python starter pipeline that pulls historical CMIP6 runs (1980–2014) and observed temperature and precipitation for West Africa, computes monthly-based extreme indices, fits GEV 20-year return levels and builds a graph of which models behave alike.

Built for the Climatematch Academy course. Historical runs only; code on GitHub, with no licence file. The Climate & DRR view →

Analysis 2023 Public

GloBox A/B test analysis

SQL queries and a Python notebook (t-tests, confidence intervals, power analysis) on whether a new banner on GloBox's mobile website paid off, from a Masterschool data-analytics sprint. The README links a Tableau Public dashboard.

Coursework. Conversion rose with the banner and spending did not, so the advice was to hold off.

Code 2025 Public

Sustainable AI Prototypes

Browser prototypes that make generative AI's energy and carbon use visible: a prompt coach and dashboard, a department display, a Tetris-style usage visual, a digital forest and a Chrome extension (v1.0). A November 2025 team project, revised after partner feedback.

My role, as its README records it: SCRUM Master & Integration Lead. The README's success metrics are targets, not results. Read the case study →

Code 2026 Public

EcoPrompt Coach — the maintained tool (promptcoach)

A JavaScript engine, web app and Chrome extension that estimate the energy, water and carbon of an LLM prompt from published benchmarks, in everyday terms. Version 2's list of models runs to September 2026; the repo links the web app.

Began as a Digital Society School prototype. Its 2026 models are extrapolated, as no lab has published a figure for one; the extension runs unpacked, in no store. Read the case study →

Tool 2026 Public

EcoPrompt Coach — this site's edition, with its evidence ledger

sustaintheworld

Interactive per-query footprint calculator, with an evidence ledger giving every emission factor a source, publication date, vintage, uncertainty range and review date. Input and output tokens are priced separately, because decode costs several times what prefill does.

Methods Published inference benchmarks · Ember grid intensities · Disclosed provider PUE/WUE

Every factor is auditable from the page itself. Its code and data are its own, separate from the maintained tool's. Read the case study →

Dataset 2026 Public

AI carbon factor set — sources, ranges and review dates

sustaintheworld

The machine-readable factor set behind the EcoPrompt Coach and the homepage's AI energy chart: ten models, thirteen grid regions, four cooling profiles, plus PUE, the token-energy model and everyday equivalents — each with a citation, a vintage and a plausible range.

Methods Literature synthesis · Provider disclosure review

Reusable on its own. A test fails the build if any factor loses its source, range or review date. Read the case study →

Field Notes

sustaintheworld

Short essays connecting the three threads: what 164 water points taught me about data, why I wrote a pessimistic future on purpose, and what to do about the footprint of a prompt.

Written for the site, not peer-reviewed.

Code 2026 Public

Journey map generator — reproducible cartography

sustaintheworld

Builds the site's journey map from Natural Earth 50 m coastlines: a region-fitted Natural Earth projection, variable simplification, and deterministic output. Pinned dependencies, and a check that the committed SVG still matches the script.

Methods d3-geo Natural Earth projection · TopoJSON variable simplification

npm run map:build to regenerate, npm run map:check to verify. Byte-identical across runs.

Hunan University

Argued that Freetown's water gap is not primarily a pipe-capacity problem, and developed demand-side, reuse and community-stewardship alternatives scoped for resource-constrained settings.

Methods Systems analysis · Feasibility assessment · Implementation framework design

Defended May 2021, on a full Chinese Government (MOFCOM) scholarship. Read the case study →

First class honours, graduated top of class. The method went on to inform real siting work. Read the case study →

Reproducing what is here

How, and the commands to run

The outputs that are part of this site run from its one clone, with no build step and no API key; each repository above says how to run it. The EcoPrompt Coach and the homepage's energy chart read one factor set, so they cannot disagree about a model. The chart shows each model's published figure for a 1,000-token answer; the coach multiplies it by data-centre overhead (PUE, 1.2 unless you change it), so for the same answer it prints 1.2 times the chart's figure. The map regenerates byte-identically from pinned dependencies. The narration is content-addressed, so re-rendering unchanged text costs nothing.

npm install && npm test
runs every suite, the map check and the asset-weight budgets
npm run map:build
regenerates the journey map from Natural Earth data
npm run map:check
proves the committed SVG still matches its generator
npm run budget
measures what a first view actually costs, asset by asset
npm run build:content
regenerates every page derived from content/
npm run voice -- --dry-run
shows what re-rendering the narration would cost, and spends nothing
